_comment: Hierarchical MILP AllGather on rail_optimized_256gpu with switch copy. 256 GPUs (32 hosts x 8), rail-optimized single plane: 8 leaves (one per rail) / 4 spines, 2:1 leaf taper, each leaf-spine edge 4 x 400Gbps cables. Hierarchical only. milp_chunking=2: one MILP chunk = 2 of a host's 8 identities for one destination-cell set, so 4 chunks per host -- between 'holder' (8, intractable here) and 'cell' (1, voids multipath across the 8 uplinks). Bundles span holder GPUs, so one GPU of each pair stages through the NVSwitch. switch_copy [true, false]: the network switches of the coarse level copy -- a fan-out is one Send, charged once on its uplink, and ncclize emits it as ONE multicast send threadblock (tb send="r1,r2") with one mscclflowid, plus a switch-JSON (format 2) entry listing every out port; the cell NVSwitches do not copy (multicast there needs NVLS). Pass --no-multicast to ncclize for the pre-multicast output (one unicast send per branch). SLOWEST_LINK keeps every coarse link at >= 1 chunk/epoch (occupancy 1: no multi-epoch legs). objective_type 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) puts makespan first; PAPER (3) ties on it. Outputs: Schedules/<prefix>_flat.json (+ _coarse/_identities/_intra side outputs). warmstart: a leaf-broadcast MIP start (makespan 16 = the ingress bound) -- generate it first with `PYTHONPATH=. python teccl/examples/hierarchy_leaf_broadcast_warmstart.py -i <this file>`, which writes warmstarts/rail_optimized_256gpu_hierarchical_allgather_milp_b2.mst; without it Gurobi found no incumbent in 4 h. num_epochs 16 IS that bound (124 chunks into 8 in-links of 1 chunk/epoch), so no horizon past it can help. objective_tier_time_limit caps the makespan tier: its relaxation bound (~7 epochs) never closes on the start's provably optimal 16, and uncapped it would take the whole time limit from the lower tiers. See teccl/hierarchy/milp_design.md and teccl/ncclize/multicast_output_design.md.
